title: Expected comparison cost
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $l$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$. The expected comparison cost is the sum, over all outcomes of the randomized kth-element search, of the probability of that outcome multiplied by its natural-number cost, regarded as an extended nonnegative real number.
